alerts.title: Creatinine recorded only as pasted text
alerts.message: A creatinine result appears only in pasted lab text, so its date is unknown. Check when it was taken and enter it as a dated lab result for a patient on TDF.

alerts.title: Missing Viral Load Monitoring Plan
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend a viral load test 3 months after ART initiation for pregnant women. The patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago and is now 22 weeks pregnant, placing her near the 3-month mark. No viral load monitoring plan is documented for this upcoming critical time point to assess initial treatment response and guide PMTCT management.

evidence.recommended_action: Order a viral load test now to align with the 3-month post-initiation guideline for pregnant women.

alerts.title: Potential DTG-Iron Interaction
alerts.message: Guidelines highlight a potential interaction between dolutegravir (DTG) and divalent cation-containing medications like iron supplements. The patient is pregnant and prescribed ferrous sulfate. This interaction can reduce DTG absorption and compromise virologic suppression. No plan documents addressing this interaction, such as dosing separation.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to take ferrous sulfate and DTG at least 6 hours apart to minimize interaction.

alerts.title: Creatinine Rise on TDF
alerts.message: Patient's creatinine increased from 0.8 mg/dL (pre-ART) to 1.1 mg/dL after 10 weeks on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), with eGFR dropping to 78 mL/min/1.73m2. TDF is associated with renal toxicity. However, pregnancy itself causes physiological changes in renal function and creatinine. The absence of proteinuria is evidence against significant glomerular injury.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor renal function closely; consider switching to TAF if creatinine continues to rise or if other risk factors emerge.

etween DTG and divalent cation-containing medication in pregnancy, since pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements and/or magnesium-/aluminium- containing antacids (see module 17). Patients returning to care in pregnancy after interrupting a first-line NNRTI regimen or those exposed to previous VTP regimens should be put directly on a DTG-based regimen, rather than retrying an NNRTI-regimen (see also module 16).
